remarks: Heavily reconstructed. Tubular slide stays; moveable slide stay telescopic, with wooden handle attached. Ferrules have crown-and-dragon’s-head pattern. Copper-colored angel’s head attached at side of bell bow (new). Flat bell stay with floral design, hinge, pin, eyelet; looks like Nuremberg work. Garland has tooth pattern at top, maker’s name and leaf pattern in center. Rim wire has raised leaf pattern. No coil in bell bow. Blows nicely. According to Waterhouse 1993: 275, Miler (also known as “Müller”) apprenticed to Simon Reichard in Nuremberg, but later moved to Vienna. Examined by the author, June 1999, at which time the instrument was being used by the Innsbrucker Bläserkreis.
